guide.summary: Museums, gardens and medina restaurants, with breakfast cafés, a Guéliz bakery, rooftop cocktail bars and luxury hotel tables checked against their own websites.
highlights: Musée des Confluences Dar El Bacha
guide.tip: Plan around closing days: the Fondation Nationale des Musées sites (Dar El Bacha, Dar Si Saïd and the Jamaâ el-Fna museum) close on Mondays, and the Musée Yves Saint Laurent closes on Wednesdays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Dar El Bacha, Dar Si Saïd and the Jamaâ el-Fna museum close on Mondays; the Musée Yves Saint Laurent and Le Foundouk close on Wednesdays. Amal Gueliz, La Famille and +61 serve lunch Monday to Saturday only.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Musée Yves Saint Laurent tickets are sold only through tickets.jardinmajorelle.com, which it calls the only official site. Maison de la Photographie tickets are not sold online and are paid on site by card or cash.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: El Fenn's roof terrace takes no reservations for drinks but has limited capacity, with last admittance at 22:30. Kabana states reservations are required, and Amal Gueliz accepts walk-ins but advises booking for busy Friday couscous day.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Comptoir Darna's dress code is smart casual, with sportswear, shorts and men's sandals not welcome. Le Jardin Secret's tower is not open to children under 6, while entry to the garden is free for under-12s.

guide.dek: Anchor each day on one museum or garden in the morning, keep Mondays for sights outside the national museum network, and book dinners and rooftop tables ahead.
intro: You can cover a lot of Marrakech's museums on foot from the medina, but closing days shape the week. The Fondation Nationale des Musées runs the Musée des Confluences Dar El Bacha, Dar Si Saïd's carpet and weaving museum and the Jamaâ el-Fna intangible heritage museum, all open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00 and closed on Mondays. Dar El Bacha is showing Enki Bilal: l'Exposition from 15 October 2026. Maison de la Photographie, on rue Ahl Fes, opens every day from 9:30 to 19:00, sells tickets on site only, and includes entry to the Musée de la Musique.

In the medina's north, Le Jardin Secret on Rue Mouassine opens daily, with October hours of 9:30 to 18:00 and November hours of 9:30 to 17:30; its tower costs extra and is closed to under-6s. Out in Guéliz, the Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech opens 10:00 to 18:00 every day except Wednesday and sells tickets only online. For contemporary art, MACAAL at Al Maaden has Daoud Aoulad-Syad's solo show until 29 November 2026 and Yassine Balbzioui's Crazy Lines until 8 January 2027. Anima Garden, on the Ourika road, runs a free shuttle from the medina.

For lunch, Amal's Guéliz centre serves Monday to Saturday from 12:00 to 15:30, and Friday is couscous day, so you should arrive early. La Famille on Riad Zitoun Jdid changes its menu daily and serves Monday to Saturday lunch, while Naranj on the same street opens daily from 12:30 to 22:30. For breakfast, Le Grand Café de la Poste takes bookings from 9:00, Pâtisserie Amandine on Rue Mohamed El Beqal opens at 8:00, and Cafe Clock in the Kasbah opens daily from 9:00 to 23:00.

Evenings run late. Terrasse des Épices serves dinner from 18:30 to 00:30 daily, Le Foundouk opens from 19:00 to midnight except Wednesdays, and Comptoir Darna in Hivernage serves nightly from 19:00 with a smart casual dress code. For drinks, El Fenn's roof terrace is open to non-residents from 12:00 to 23:00 without reservations, though capacity is limited. La Sultana runs a 6 p.m. sunset mixology workshop for up to four people, and Kabana opens daily until 2:00 with reservations required.
summaryCards: Start with Le Jardin Secret and the Jamaâ el-Fna museum in the medina, then head to the Musée Yves Saint Laurent on any day but Wednesday.
Have breakfast at Pâtisserie Amandine from 8:00 or Le Grand Café de la Poste from 9:00, then walk to Maison de la Photographie, open daily from 9:30.
Remember that the national museums close on Mondays, YSL tickets are online only, and Kabana and the larger dinner venues take reservations.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability, and hours may change for Ramadan and the Aid holidays. The Jardin Majorelle's site published hours but no street address on the pages that loaded, and its contact and French pages failed (HTTP 429/500), so it is not included. Several sites could not be read because of certificate or connection errors (Nomad, Le Jardin, L'Mida, Dar Moha, Pepe Nero, Musée de Marrakech, Kechmara, Four Seasons). Weekly hours were not published for La Mamounia, Royal Mansour, Al Fassia Aguedal, Le Trou au Mur, La Maison Arabe or MACAAL, and Pâtisserie Amandine did not state closing days. The end date of the Enki Bilal exhibition at Dar El Bacha was not published.
